test.name: A cluster no single fact explains reads as a merged profile
test.description: The counterpart to ut_check_warnings_009. The tool returns two contradictions on Patrick whose facts are disjoint by construction: hasChristeningBeforeBirth cites the Christening and Birth facts (F5, F1), hasBurialBeforeDeath cites the Burial and Death facts (F6, F2). Because no one fact is implicated in both, the shared-cause reading the agent body asks the skill to test first is unavailable, and the merged-profile reading is the stronger one -- the branch the agent body gates on exactly this case. Before this test nothing in the suite exercised it: person-warnings-cluster.json is the only other multi-contradiction fixture and all of its warnings on Patrick share F2, so a regression on the disjoint branch would have passed the whole suite (Mercy Okum's review of #1896, finding 7). hasEventAfterDeath1 is deliberately absent: it cites every fact the person has, so it can never establish disjointness.

input.delegation:
Run a thorough warnings check on Cornelius Brady.

personId: I1

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Should call person_warnings with personId 'I1' and report both contradictions the tool returned.
Should recognize the two contradictions as a cluster on one person rather than two independent items, and should test the shared-cause reading first as the agent body requires.

Should conclude that NO single wrong fact explains this cluster, and should reach that from the facts: hasChristeningBeforeBirth cites F5 and F1, hasBurialBeforeDeath cites F6 and F2, which are disjoint. Crediting the conclusion is what matters; naming the facts explicitly is a plus, not a requirement. Do NOT credit or require any claim that a particular direction of date error fires particular tags -- no such claim is correct.

Should treat the merged-profile reading as the stronger one here, and say so. This is the one branch where asserting that reading is correct -- unlike ut_check_warnings_009, hedging toward 'these may share a single cause' is wrong, because the facts rule it out.

Should recommend the chronological timeline rebuild and split-point search, which the agent body gates on precisely this case. Phrase it as a research action the user can take: naming an internal skill in user-facing text is itself a defect under the skill's phrasing rule.

Should classify both warnings as Contradiction, the tier the tool returned (severity: "contradiction"), and pair them with the Fundamental assumption category -- Appendix C of the agent body maps Fundamental to severity "contradiction". Labelling a "contradiction" as the Valid category is a Severity classification defect. The tier names "Critical" and "Note" were retired by PR #1545 -- do not require them.
